body: Cement is a regional, heavy, low-value product that can travel only ~300–500 km by road. Profit is EBITDA per tonne: realisation minus energy (pet coke, coal and power, ~25–30% of cost), freight (~25–30%) and raw materials, times volumes. Pricing depends on regional supply discipline. Key metrics: EBITDA/tonne (~₹900–1,300 normal, ₹1,400+ peak), capacity utilisation (~65–75% industry), realisation per tonne, cost per tonne (power and fuel, freight, lead distance), volume growth against the industry, trade/premium share, net debt/EBITDA, capex per tonne (~$80–120/t greenfield) and market share. Cycle drivers: housing, infrastructure and rural demand; supply additions (consolidation: UltraTech plus Adani now hold ~50%+ capacity), fuel prices, the monsoon (Jul–Sep weakest quarter) and pre-election construction. Lead indicators: the cement index in the eight-core-industries data (monthly), dealer price checks (brokers' monthly channel checks), pet coke prices, state capex, and the Ministry of Commerce/DPIIT production index. Winners (Shree Cement on cost leadership, UltraTech on scale and acquisitions, Dalmia in the East) had the lowest-quartile cost and lead distance, captive power and green energy, and disciplined capacity addition in their regions. Losers were high-cost single-plant players and over-leveraged acquirers (Jaiprakash Associates). Valuation: EV/EBITDA 12–20x or EV per tonne of capacity ($100–200/t; replacement cost ~$80–120/t). Nov 2026: UltraTech's Q2 FY27 EBITDA/tonne was ₹974, down ~20% QoQ on fuel cost but up ₹60 YoY, with volumes +13.8% and utilisation 71%. Prices rose 7–10%/bag in late September and ~5% further in October. Traps: capacity wars and paying replacement-cost multiples at peak margins.

data.business_model: Regional bulk commodity; EBITDA/tonne x volume; pricing power from regional consolidation.
data.current_state_nov_2026: UltraTech Q2 FY27: EBITDA/t ₹974 (−~20% QoQ, +₹60 YoY), domestic volume +13.8%, utilisation 71% (66%), PAT +21.3%. Ambuja total cost ₹4,410/t (₹4,182 ex-geopolitical fuel impact). Prices +7–10%/bag in late September, October ~5% above Q2 average. CRISIL saw FY27 EBITDA/t at ₹925–950 vs ~₹1,000 FY26.
data.cycle_drivers: Housing/infra demand, regional supply additions, fuel prices, monsoon seasonality, consolidation (M&A pricing discipline), elections.
key_metrics: Cost/tonne: power & fuel, freight, lead distance
EV per tonne & capex per tonne
lead_indicators: Eight core industries – cement (monthly, Office of Economic Adviser)
Broker dealer channel checks (monthly price per bag)
data.valuation: EV/EBITDA 12–20x through cycle; EV/t $100–200 (consolidation M&A ~$130–170/t in 2022–25). Peaks: 2007, 2017, 2021. Troughs: 2012–14, 2019.
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Limestone (captive mines) -> clinker (energy intensive) -> grinding -> dealers/trade (~70%) and non-trade/institutional. Margins sit with low-cost producers that have captive limestone, WHRS/green power and short lead distance; dealers hold thin margins.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: cost leadership (fuel, freight, green power), regional dominance, disciplined M&A, low leverage. Losers: high-cost single-region players, debt-funded expansion into oversupply, acquisitions paid at peak EV/t.

title: Sector playbook: Indian cement
